title: Wedding Guest Book Alternatives: 25 Ideas With Costs
description: 25 wedding guest book alternatives, from instant-camera and audio guest books to Jenga blocks and globes, with rough costs, effort and what you keep.
dek: Photo, audio, keepsake and written ideas, with costs and a tip for each one.
excerpt: Instant-camera books, audio phones, puzzle pieces, globes, advice jars and 20 more wedding guest book alternatives, with rough costs, effort and a pick-by-personality table.

faq.q: What can I use instead of a wedding guest book?
faq.a: Good alternatives include an instant-camera photo book, a photo booth strip album, an audio guest book phone, and objects guests sign, like Jenga blocks, puzzle pieces, a globe or a framed print. Written options such as advice cards or date-night ideas work well too. Choose based on where it will live afterward and how long each guest will spend on it.

faq.q: How much does an audio guest book cost?
faq.a: As of November 2026, the rental listings we checked ran from about $100 for a basic local package to $299 and up for a shipped vintage-phone service. Check what’s included: delivery or shipping, how you receive the recordings (download, USB or vinyl) and whether extras cost more. Buying your own phone is another option if you want to keep it.

faq.q: How do you set up a Polaroid or instant-camera guest book?
faq.a: Put an instant camera, enough film for about one print per guest plus spares, a blank album, photo corners or double-sided tape and a fine-tip permanent marker on one table. Add a small sign with the steps: take a photo, write a note beside it, stick it in. Ask one friend to restock film and keep things moving.

faq.q: Do you need a wedding guest book at all?
faq.a: No. A guest book is a tradition, not a requirement, so skip it if nothing about it appeals to you. If you want one, choose something you’ll display or revisit, because a book that sits in a closet isn’t worth the table space. A shared photo album from the day can serve the same purpose with no extra station.

faq.q: What is the cheapest wedding guest book alternative?
faq.a: A book you already love, an advice-card jar, holiday ornaments or signing the welcome sign you already bought usually cost under $50 in total. Craft-store river rocks with paint markers are cheap too. The most expensive choices tend to be rented services such as audio phones and photo booths.
